source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice long questions written from Chapter 3 (PDF 68-89), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 3 (Algorithms and Problem Solving) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 8 number ka hai (definition, misalon ke saath wazahat, farq, program likh kar samjhana), aksar definition aur wazahat ke hisson mein (jaise 2 + 3 x 2). Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Computer science starts by describing problems clearly. (i) Define a computational problem and explain its input, process and output. (3) (ii) Explain the four common classes of computational problems with one example of each. (5) (8 marks)
(Computer science masail ko wazeh bayan karne se shuru hoti hai. (i) Computational problem ki definition aur is ke input, process aur output wazeh karein. (ii) Computational problems ki chaar aam qisamen misaalon ke sath wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Computational problem woh masla hai jo computational process, yani computer par chalne wale qadam ba qadam algorithm se hal ho; hal mehdood qadmon se milta hai.
1. Input: algorithm ko diya gaya data.
2. Process: input par lagaye gaye qadam ya usool.
3. Output: process ke baad milne wala nateeja.
Misaal: number juft hai ya nahin: input aik integer, process 2 se taqseem, output even ya odd.

(ii) 1. Decision problems: output haan ya na, jaise number juft hai?
2. Search problems: shart poori karne wali cheez dhoondna, jaise list mein Islamabad.
3. Optimization problems: behtareen hal, jaise har college se guzarne wala sab se chhota raasta.
4. Counting problems: ginna ke shiraait kitne tareeqon se poori hon, jaise cities ke darmiyan mumkina raaste.

blocks.prompt:
2 Generate and Test is a simple problem-solving approach. (i) Describe the Generate and Test algorithm and the scenarios in which it is particularly useful. (3) (ii) Explain three advantages and three disadvantages of Generate and Test. (5) (8 marks)
(Generate and Test masla hal karne ka saada tareeqa hai. (i) Is algorithm ko aur un suraton ko bayan karein jahan yeh mufeed hai. (ii) Is ke teen faide aur teen khamiyan wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Generate and Test seedha tareeqa hai: mumkina hal (randomly, systematically ya heuristic se) banata hai aur har aik ko shiraait par parakhta hai; sab shiraait poori ho to hal durust, warna naya hal. Durust hal milne ya sab hal khatam hone tak chalta hai.
Mufeed: chhota problem space; wazeh hikmat-e-amli na ho aur sab dekhna zaroori ho; heuristics se tadaad kam ho sake.

(ii) Faide:
1. Saadgi: samajhna aur banana aasan.
2. Wasee istemal: bohat se masail par.
3. Exhaustiveness: koi hal reh nahin jata.
Khamiyan (Cons):
1. Susti: bare problem space mein bohat se hal parakhne parte hain.
2. Behtareen hal ki zamanat nahin, sirf durust hal.
3. Mehngai: bohat zyada hal hon to na-qabil-e-amal.

book_ref.quote: Versatility: It can be applied to a wide range of problems, particularly when no clear solution strategy exists

blocks.prompt:
3 Before solving a problem we ask whether it can be solved and how fast. (i) Differentiate between solvable and unsolvable problems with one example each. (4) (ii) Explain why the Travelling Salesman Problem is intractable, finding the number of possible routes for 3, 4, 5 and 6 cities. (4) (8 marks)
(Masla hal karne se pehle dekhte hain ke yeh hal ho sakta hai ya nahin aur kitni jaldi. (i) Solvable aur unsolvable masail mein misaalon ke sath farq likhein. (ii) Wazeh karein ke TSP intractable kyon hai aur 3, 4, 5 aur 6 cities ke raaste nikalein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Masla solvable ya unsolvable is par hai ke us ka algorithm mojood hai ya nahin (table dekhein).

(ii) Polynomial time mein hal hone wale masail tractable hain; intractable ko super-polynomial (aksar exponential) waqt chahiye.
TSP: cities se guzar kar wapas aane wala sab se chhota raasta. Yeh NP-hard hai; raaste factorial (n!) barhte hain:
3 cities: 6; 4 cities: 24; 5 cities: 120; 6 cities: 720 raaste.
Raaste bohat tezi se barhte hain (10 cities par 3,628,800), is liye bare masail ka theek hal na-mumkin sa hai; yeh intractable hai.

book_ref.quote: The problem is NP-hard, meaning that as the number of cities increases, the number of possible routes grows factorially

rows: Algorithm mehdood waqt mein hal kar deta hai.
Har surat ke liye koi algorithm nahin ban sakta.
Wazeh input, output aur qadam ba qadam tareeqa.
Har input ke liye zamanat wala aam tareeqa nahin.
Misaal: Halting Problem; Alan Turing ne sabit kiya.

blocks.prompt:
4 Complexity classes describe how hard problems are. (i) Explain Class P using the example of sorting the list [4, 1, 3, 2, 5]. (4) (ii) Explain Class NP using the example of Sudoku. (4) (8 marks)
(Complexity classes batati hain ke masail kitne mushkil hain. (i) List [4, 1, 3, 2, 5] sort karne ki misaal se Class P wazeh karein. (ii) Sudoku ki misaal se Class NP wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Class P: woh masail jo computer mo'assar tareeqe se jaldi hal kar le, masla bara ho tab bhi.
Misaal: [4, 1, 3, 2, 5] ko [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] banana.
1. Hal aasan: list barhne par waqt qabil-e-intezam raftaar se barhta hai.
2. Polynomial time: list dugni to waqt taqreeban dugna.
3. Deterministic algorithm: compare aur swap ke wazeh qadam hamesha durust nateeja dete hain.

(ii) Class NP: diya gaya hal jaldi jaancha ja sake magar dhoondna mushkil ho.
Misaal: Sudoku, 9 × 9 grid ki har row, column aur 3 × 3 sub-grid mein 1 se 9 aik dafa.
1. Jaanch aasan: mukammal grid ki rows, columns aur sub-grids jaldi dekh li jati hain.
2. Hal mushkil: shuru se hal karne ka koi tez yaqeeni tareeqa nahin; bohat trial and error.
3. Non-deterministic polynomial time: hal mile to jaanch jaldi, dhoondne mein bohat waqt lag sakta hai.

book_ref.quote: Verification is Easy: If someone gives you a completed Sudoku grid, you can quickly check if the solution is correct

blocks.prompt:
5 Big O notation compares how algorithms grow. (i) Define Big O notation. (2) (ii) Explain O(1), O(n), O(n²) and O(log n) time with the chapter's college examples. (6) (8 marks)
(Big O notation algorithms ki barhotri ka muqabla karti hai. (i) Big O ki definition likhein. (ii) O(1), O(n), O(n²) aur O(log n) time chapter ki college misaalon se wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Big O notation algorithm ki time complexity ka riyazi bayan hai; input barhne par waqt ki upari had batati hai aur algorithms ka muqabla aasan karti hai.

(ii) 1. O(1): waqt input se nahin badalta; index se array item lena; graph par sapaat line.
2. O(n): waqt input ke sath seedha barhta hai; n talaba ki IDs aik aik kar ke dekhna, bad tareen surat mein sab n.
3. O(n²): har talib-e-ilm ka har doosre se muqabla; comparisons n(n − 1)/2, is liye O(n²).
4. O(log n): andaze ka khel; har andaza beech se, jawab range aadhi kar deta hai; O(log n).

book_ref.quote: This notation helps in comparing the efficiency of different algorithms by giving a clear picture of their performance

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Kitab comparisons n(n − 1) likhti hai; durust tadaad n(n − 1)/2 hai kyon ke har jora sirf aik dafa compare hota hai. Complexity phir bhi O(n²) hi rehti hai.

blocks.prompt:
6 Compare the growth of common time complexities. For n = 8, 16 and 1024, find log₂ n, n, n log₂ n and n², and the number of pair comparisons n(n − 1)/2. State which complexity is best and which is worst for large n. (8 marks)
(Aam time complexities ki barhotri ka muqabla karein. n = 8, 16 aur 1024 ke liye log₂ n, n, n log₂ n, n² aur n(n − 1)/2 nikalein. Bare n ke liye behtareen aur bad tareen complexity batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Har n ke liye har expression nikalein aur dekhein ke n barhne par values kitni tezi se barhti hain (O(1) har n par wohi).

book_ref.quote: When comparing different time complexities, it

steps: n = 8: log₂ n = 3; n = 8; n log₂ n = 24; n² = 64; pairs = 28.
n = 16: log₂ n = 4; n = 16; n log₂ n = 64; n² = 256; pairs = 120.
n 8 se 1024 hone par log₂ n sirf 3 se 10, n 128 guna, magar n² 64 se das lakh se zyada.
Bare input par O(1) aur O(log n) behtareen, O(n) aur O(n log n) qabil-e-intezam, aur O(n²) sab se tez barhta hai, yani bad tareen.
blocks.final_answer: n = 1024 par: 10, 10,240, 1,048,576 aur 523,776; O(1)/O(log n) behtareen, O(n²) bad tareen.

blocks.prompt:
7 Algorithms also need memory. (i) Define space complexity and explain why it matters. (2) (ii) Explain O(1), O(n), O(n²) and O(log n) space with an example of each. (6) (8 marks)
(Algorithms ko memory bhi chahiye. (i) Space complexity ki definition aur ahmiyat likhein. (ii) O(1), O(n), O(n²) aur O(log n) space misaalon ke sath wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Space complexity naapti hai ke input barhne par algorithm ki memory kaise badalti hai, jaise barhti list ke liye kitni memory. Yeh memory ki zaroorat batati hai; bari applications aur kam memory wale systems mein bohat aham.

(ii) Yeh bhi Big O mein upari had ke tor par likhi jati hai:
1. O(1): mehdood memory, jaise sirf chand variables.
2. O(n): memory input ke sath seedhi barhti hai, jaise items ki list.
3. O(n²): n × n matrix, elements n² ke sath.
4. O(log n): bohat aahista barhti hai, jaise kuch divide-and-conquer algorithms jo har qadam par thora data rakhte hain.

book_ref.quote: Space complexity is typically expressed using Big O notation, similar to time complexity

blocks.prompt:
8 A good algorithm must suit the data and the problem. (i) Explain algorithm efficiency with the example of Bubble Sort and Merge Sort. (3) (ii) Explain scalability. (2) (iii) Explain suitability for specific problems with the book-search example. (3) (8 marks)
(Achha algorithm data aur masle ke mutabiq hona chahiye. (i) Bubble Sort aur Merge Sort ki misaal se efficiency wazeh karein. (ii) Scalability wazeh karein. (iii) Kitab dhoondne ki misaal se suitability wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Efficiency: algorithm waqt aur memory ka kitna achha istemal karta hai; time aur space complexity se jaancha jata hai.
Misaal: Bubble Sort O(n²): input dugna to waqt chaar guna. Merge Sort O(n log n) bohat aahista barhta hai, bare data ke liye behtar.

(ii) Scalability: input barhne par bhi efficiency barqarar rakhna, chahe data shuru ke andaze se kahin bara ho.

(iii) Har algorithm har masle ke liye nahin; chunao raftaar, memory ya data ki noiyat par.
Misaal: chhote be-tarteeb majmooe mein har kitab dekhein (Linear Search); alphabetical shelf par beech se shuru kar ke aadha chunein (Binary Search).

book_ref.quote: The efficiency of an algorithm is typically evaluated based on its time complexity

blocks.prompt:
9 Explain the Divide and Conquer technique and sort the list [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] with Merge Sort, showing every divide and merge step. (8 marks)
(Divide and Conquer technique wazeh karein aur list [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] ko Merge Sort se sort karein, har divide aur merge qadam dikhayein.)
blocks.explanation: Divide and Conquer bare masle ko chhote hisson mein torta hai, har hissa alag hal kar ke hal jorta hai. Merge Sort list ko do hisson mein baant kar har hissa sort kar ke milata hai.

book_ref.quote: Divide and Conquer is a powerful algorithm design technique that works by breaking a large problem into smaller, more manageable parts

blocks.prompt:
10 Explain greedy algorithms and optimal substructure. Using the greedy Coin Change method, make 87 rupees with coins of 50, 20, 10, 5 and 1 rupees, then make 6 with coins of 4, 3 and 1, and comment on whether greedy always gives the fewest coins. (8 marks)
(Greedy algorithms aur optimal substructure wazeh karein. Greedy Coin Change se 50, 20, 10, 5 aur 1 ke sikkon se 87 rupay, phir 4, 3 aur 1 ke sikkon se 6 banayein, aur batayein ke kya greedy hamesha kam se kam sikke deta hai.)
blocks.explanation: Greedy algorithms har qadam par us waqt ka behtareen faisla karte hain is umeed par ke poora hal behtareen ho; optimal substructure wale masail mein istemal hote hain. Coin Change: har dafa bachi raqam se bara na ho aisa sab se bara sikka lein, ghatayein aur dohrayein.

book_ref.quote: The greedy algorithm would involve choosing the largest denomination coin that does not exceed the remaining amount

steps: 87: 50 lein, baqi 37.
7: 5, baqi 2; 2: 1, baqi 1; 1: 1, baqi 0.
4, 3, 1 se 6: 4 (baqi 2), phir 1 aur 1: 3 sikke.
Magar 3 + 3 = 6 sirf 2 sikke hain, yahan greedy behtareen nahin.
Greedy tez aur aasan hai magar hamesha behtareen hal ki zamanat nahin, is liye pehle masle ka tajziya zaroori hai.
blocks.final_answer: 87 = 6 sikke; 6 ke liye greedy 3 sikke deta hai jab ke 2 (3 + 3) behtareen hain.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Greedy har qadam par sirf us waqt ka sab se bara sikka dekhta hai, aage ka nahin sochta. Isi liye 6 ke liye pehle 4 le kar phans jata hai, jab ke do 3 behtar thay. Chapter ki Tidbit bhi yahi kehti hai ke greedy hamesha optimal nahin.

blocks.prompt:
11 Explain Dynamic Programming and write the steps of a Dynamic Programming method that finds the Fibonacci sequence up to the 20th term (first term 0) by storing each term. Give the stored terms. (8 marks)
(Dynamic Programming wazeh karein aur Fibonacci sequence ko 20th term tak (pehli term 0) har term mehfooz kar ke nikalne ke qadam likhein. Mehfooz terms dein.)
blocks.explanation: Dynamic Programming masle ko chhote masail mein tor kar un ke nataij mehfooz karti hai taa ke dobara hisab na ho. Fibonacci mein har term pichhli do ka jama hai; DP har term bante hi mehfooz karta hai.

book_ref.quote: Implement a dynamic programming algorithm to solve the Fibonacci sequence up to the 20th term

steps: Terms ke liye table F banayein; F(1) = 0 aur F(2) = 1 rakhein.
k = 3 se 20 tak: F(k) = F(k − 1) + F(k − 2), table se le kar, aur F(k) mehfooz karein.
Har term sirf aik dafa nikalti hai (18 jama), kyon ke pichhli terms table se milti hain, dobara nahin nikalni partin.

blocks.prompt:
12 Explain Selection Sort and sort [64, 25, 12, 22, 11] in ascending order, showing the list after each pass. State its time complexity. (8 marks)
(Selection Sort wazeh karein aur [64, 25, 12, 22, 11] ko barhti tarteeb mein sort karein, har pass ke baad list dikhayein. Time complexity batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Selection Sort unsorted hisse ka sab se chhota element chun kar pehle unsorted element se swap karta hai aur had aik qadam aage karta hai.

book_ref.quote: Find the minimum element in the unsorted part of the list

steps: Pass 4: [25, 64] mein 25 pehle hi aage; koi tabdeeli nahin: [11, 12, 22, 25, 64].
Time complexity O(n²); Bubble Sort ki tarah bare data ke liye sust magar aasan.

blocks.prompt:
13 Algorithms are step-by-step procedures. (i) Define an algorithm and give two reasons why algorithms are important. (3) (ii) Explain linear search with its steps, show how it finds Faisalabad in [Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Faisalabad], and state its worst case and time complexity. (5) (8 marks)
(Algorithms qadam ba qadam tareeqe hain. (i) Algorithm ki definition aur ahmiyat ki do wajoohat likhein. (ii) Linear search ke qadam likhein, [Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Faisalabad] mein Faisalabad dhoondna dikhayein, aur worst case aur time complexity batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Algorithm masla hal karne ka qadam ba qadam tareeqa hai, jaise recipe. Ahmiyat:
1. Yeh computer science ki bunyad hain aur software ki mantiq dete hain.
2. In se mushkil masail hal, performance behtar aur durusti yaqeeni hoti hai (jaise Google ka PageRank).

(ii) Linear search har item aik aik kar ke dekhti hai.
Qadam: 1. Pehle item se shuru. 2. Matloob item ko mojooda se milana. 3. Na mile to agla item. 4. Milne ya list khatam hone tak dohrana.
Faisalabad: Karachi (nahin), Lahore (nahin), Islamabad (nahin), Faisalabad (mil gaya): 4 dafa.
Worst case: item aakhri ho ya mojood na ho, sab n items dekhne parte hain.
Time complexity: O(n).

book_ref.quote: This method is called a linear search because you check each item in a straight line

blocks.prompt:
14 Explain Binary Search. On the sorted list [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 56, 72, 91] (positions 1 to 10, take the lower middle), trace the search for 23 and for 60, and state the time complexity. (8 marks)
(Binary Search wazeh karein. Sorted list [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 56, 72, 91] (positions 1 se 10, neeche wala beech) mein 23 aur 60 ki search trace karein aur time complexity batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Binary Search sorted list par: beech wala dekhein; target ho to rukein; chhota ho to baayan aadha, bara ho to daayan; milne ya interval khaali hone tak dohrayein.

book_ref.quote: It works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half and discarding the half where the item cannot be, until the item is found or the interval is empty

steps: 23: positions 1-10, beech position 5 = 16; 23 bara, positions 6-10.
Positions 6-10, beech position 8 = 56; 23 chhota, positions 6-7.
Positions 6-7, beech position 6 = 23: 3 comparisons mein position 6 par mil gaya.
Positions 9-10, beech position 9 = 72; 60 chhota, interval khaali: 60 list mein nahin (3 comparisons).
Har comparison interval aadha karta hai, is liye O(log n).
blocks.final_answer: 23 position 6 par (16, 56, 23); 60 mojood nahin (16, 56, 72); O(log n).

blocks.prompt:
15 A graph has edges A-B, A-C, B-D, B-E and C-F. Starting at A, trace Breadth-First Search (with a queue) and Depth-First Search (with a stack), showing the queue or stack after each node is processed. Take neighbours in alphabetical order; for DFS push them in reverse order so the alphabetically first is popped first. (8 marks)
(Graph ke edges A-B, A-C, B-D, B-E aur C-F hain. A se BFS (queue) aur DFS (stack) trace karein, har node ke baad queue ya stack dikhayein. Padosi alphabetical; DFS mein ulti tarteeb se push karein taa ke pehla alphabetical pehle pop ho.)
blocks.explanation: BFS: root enqueue; node dequeue, process, unvisited padosi enqueue; queue khaali hone tak (level ba level). DFS: root push; node pop, process, unvisited padosi push; stack khaali hone tak (pehle gehrai, phir wapsi).

book_ref.quote: Repeat the process until the stack is empty

steps: BFS: queue [A]. A process, B, C enqueue: [B, C].
BFS: B process, D, E enqueue: [C, D, E]. C process, F enqueue: [D, E, F].
BFS: D, E, F baari baari (naye padosi nahin); queue khaali. BFS tarteeb: A, B, C, D, E, F.
DFS: stack [A]. A pop, C phir B push: [C, B] (B upar).
DFS: B pop, E phir D push: [C, E, D]. D pop: [C, E]. E pop: [C].
DFS: C pop, F push: [F]. F pop: stack khaali. DFS tarteeb: A, B, D, E, C, F.
BFS level ba level chalta hai, DFS pehle A-B-D shakh mein neeche jata hai aur phir wapas aata hai. Dono O(V + E).
blocks.final_answer: BFS: A, B, C, D, E, F. DFS: A, B, D, E, C, F.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Queue mein jo pehle aaye woh pehle nikalta hai (FIFO), is liye BFS qareeb wale nodes pehle dekhta hai. Stack mein jo aakhir mein aaye woh pehle nikalta hai (LIFO), is liye DFS naye node ke padosi foran dekhta hai aur gehra chala jata hai.
